subject: POC checklist: observability & evals requirements for Finlytics
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Evans <sam.evans@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: POC checklist: observability & evals requirements for Finlytics

Hi Sam / Priya — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum for the POC. Bold items are asks from your side.

Summary of pain points you shared
- Unpredictable token cost and latency across peak inference traffic, impacting SLAs for near-real-time features.
- No centralized visibility across models (hosted vs. on-prem) — ops teams struggle to correlate degraded outputs with infra events.
- Lack of regression detection on model output quality when swapping model variants or quantizing.

What success looks like for Finlytics (we heard)
- Observability: per-route dashboards (latency P50/P95/P99, token cost/breakdown, error rates) and a tracing hook into requests to join model spans with downstream services.
- Evals: a curated golden prompt set + automatic regression alerts when pass rates drop >5% for a given prompt cohort.
- Rollout safety: canary rollouts with automatic fallback to a stable variant on latency/SLA breaches.

Current stack you mentioned
- Inference: mix of managed endpoints + an on-prem GPU pool for sensitive workloads.
- Telemetry: Prometheus + DataDog for infra metrics, but no structured model-level traces.
- CI: internal ML infra with S3 test buckets and a limited eval harness.

Technical asks we can cover in the POC (proposed)
- Dashboard spec: we will provision a demo dashboard with token-level cost, per-model latency histograms, and top failure traces. Please confirm 3 canonical routes you want instrumented during the POC.
- Tracing hooks: we can add a lightweight header-based trace that maps request -> model_variant -> device; need a contact for your infra team to whitelist our tracing headers.
- Golden prompts: please share your top 50 prompt+expected-output pairs (or let us pull a redacted sample from S3).
- Regression alerts: we will wire up a threshold-based alert and a weekly report that shows pass/fail deltas.

Next steps (timeline)
1) You share the 3 POC routes + 50 golden prompts (by Wed 4/21).
2) We spin up a sandbox with dashboards + tracing hooks (target Fri 4/23).
3) Kickoff POC run and initial evals (week of 4/26).

Attachments: redwood-poc-checklist.xlsx (detailed checklist), redwood-poc-sla-draft.pdf (SLA template).

Open questions for you
- Is the POC allowed to run with a small snapshot of production traffic, or do we need to use synthetic traffic only?
- Who should be our engineering point-of-contact for tracing header and VPC egress (name + email)?

If that summary looks right I’ll schedule the 30-minute kickoff for Fri 4/23 and loop in our infra lead Markus for the tracing integration.

Thanks — Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Sam Evans <sam.evans@finlytics.ai>

Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 16:42:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: POC checklist: observability & evals requirements for Finlytics

Thanks Aditya — this is great and aligns with our notes. Clarifications below.

On the 3 routes: please instrument these endpoints: /api/v1/transaction/normalize, /api/v1/summary/generate, and /api/v1/alerts/classify. Those cover the latency-sensitive flow, the heavy batching flow, and the NLU safety filter respectively.

Golden prompts: we’ll provide a redacted S3 manifest with 60 prompt examples (we prefer you pick 50). I’ll share the S3 path by EOD Tue 4/20. Is role-based access required for Redwood’s sandbox service account?

Traffic for POC: we’re ok with a small production-sampled traffic for the latency experiments (up to 5% of traffic), but for evals and golden prompts use our synthetic harness. We’ll confirm formally with security but wanted to give a green light in principle.

Our infra contact: Priya Shah (CTO) — cc’d. Priya, can you confirm the process for whitelisting headers and whether we can create a temporary service account for Redwood?

Appreciate the clear next steps. One ask from our side: can you include a short cost projection for the expected POC run (estimated tokens and cost delta for quantized vs. float runs)?

—Sam
Sam Evans
Head of ML | Finlytics
sam.evans@finlytics.ai | +1 617-555-0199

Subject: Re: POC checklist: observability & evals requirements for Finlytics

Hi Sam — Monica from Solutions Architecture here. A couple of quick technical notes and a tiny ask so we can scope the tracing/dashboard work accurately.

Tracing hooks
- We plan to emit a model_span that includes: model_name, model_variant, device_id, request_id, and token_count. This will be mapped to your existing trace context (W3C traceparent). If you have a custom trace header let us know.
- For on-prem GPUs we’ll deploy a small sidecar collector that forwards spans to a temporary DataDog endpoint you provide. That requires a single egress rule and an allowlist for the collector IP.

Dashboards & metrics
- We’ll include: P50/P95/P99 latency per-route, token cost breakdown (generation vs. prompt), and a top-20 error-by-exception chart. For evals we’ll add a golden-prompt pass-rate chart with diffs per rollout.

Quality/regression alerts
- Default rule: alert when a prompt cohort’s pass-rate drops by >= 5% vs baseline for 3 consecutive runs. We can tune to your preference; confirm whether a weekly summary email is desired.

Attachments: I uploaded a starter dashboard spec and the tracer configuration sample to the shared Drive (see link below). Also attaching a minimal checklist (redwood-poc-checklist.xlsx) for your infra team.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/finlytics-poc-observability

Small ask for your infra team
- Please provide a sample request header (sanitized) so we can validate token_count extraction.

If that all sounds good I’ll block time with Markus next week to run through the sidecar deployment plan.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
